subject: Human Body
title: Pain Pathways
description: A quick, practical guide to Pain Pathways.

hook.text: Pain isn't at the injury. It's manufactured in your brain. The body sends data; the brain creates the suffering.

buildup.text: Nociceptors detect damage and send signals through nerves to the spinal cord, then up to the brain.

discovery.text: Two speeds exist: fast sharp pain travels via myelinated fibers; slow burning pain uses unmyelinated ones.

twist.text: Phantom limb pain proves the brain creates pain. Amputees feel agony in limbs that no longer exist.

climax.text: Gate control theory says non-painful input can close the pain gate. Rubbing a bump actually reduces pain signals.

punchline.text: Pain isn't where you hurt. It's where you think.

quiz.question: Why do amputees feel phantom limb pain?
options: Nerves at the stump send false signals
The brain creates pain in areas that no longer exist
Blood flow changes redirect pain to other areas
